lines.text: אזר 30 אח
אזר
* אָזַר fut. יֶאְזֹר Jer. 1, 17, c. suff. יַאְזְרֵנִי
Job 30, 18, to gird, to bind around;
also to gird oneself, to be girded. Arab.
أَزَرَ to be strong, robust, but doubtful
whether also pr. to be girded; Conj. II
to gird, Conj. III to strengthen, to aid.
Kindred roots, which all have the force
of binding around or together, girding,
surrounding, are אָסַר, אָצַר [אָצַל], עָצַר,
גָּדַר, חָדַר, חָצַר; עָזַר, עָטַר. — Spoken:
a) Of a garment with which one is
girded, c. acc. of pers. Job 30, 18. b)
With acc. of the member girded, Job 38,
3 אֱזָר־נָא חֲלָצֶיךָ gird up now thy loins.
40, 2. Jer. 1, 17. c) With acc. of the
girdle or garment with which one is
girded, only trop. 1 Sam. 2, 4 אָזְרוּ חָיִל
they gird on strength.
Niph. part. נֶאְזָר girded Ps. 65, 7.
Piel to gird, with acc. of pers. and
also of the girdle, Ps. 18, 33. 40 וַתְּאַזְּרֵנִי
חַיִל לַמִּלְחָמָה thou hast girded me with
strength for the battle. 30, 12 וַתְּאַזְּרֵנִי
שִׂמְחָה thou hast girded [or surrounded]
me with gladness. Is. 50, 11 מְאַזְּרֵי זִיקוֹת
girded i. e. armed with burning wea-
pons.—For the construction of such
verbs with two accusatives, see Lehrg.
Hithpa. to gird oneself, e. g. for bat-
tle, to arm oneself, Is. 8, 9; c. acc. trop.
Deriv. אֵזוֹר.
אֶזְרוֹעַ i. q. זְרוֹעַ, the arm, (Aleph
prosthet. see p. 1,) Jer. 32, 21. Job 31,
אֶזְרָח m. for זֶרַח with Aleph pros-
thetic. R. זָרַח no. 2. c.
1. a native tree, growing in its own
soil, not transplanted, Ps. 37, 35.—
Hence
2. Of persons, a native, one born in
the country, not a foreigner, Lev. 16,
אֶזְרָחִי patronym. an Ezrahite, one
of the descendants of Ezrah, אֶזְרָח;
spoken of Ethan, 1 K. 5, 11 [4, 31]. Ps.
89, 1; also of Heman Ps. 88, 1. In
1 Chr. 2, 6 both these are said to be
descendants of Zerah, זֶרַח, the son of
Judah; so that we may regard אֶזְרָח as
another form of the same name, found
only in the patronymic.
* I. אָח constr. אֲחִי, c. suff. אָחִי (my
brother), אָחִיךָ, אֲחִיכֶם; Plur. אַחִים
(Dag. impl.) constr. אֲחֵי, c. suff. אַחֶיךָ,
אֲחֵיכֶם, c. suff. 3 pers. אֶחָיו for אֲחָיו,
comp. Lehrg. p. 602.
1. a brother, undoubtedly a primitive
word, Arab. أَخٌ, st. constr. أَخُو, أَخِى,
أَخَا; Syr. ܐܰܚܳܐ, Chald. אַח. It follows
partly the analogy of verbs ל״ה, and
partly that of verbs ע״ע; comp. Lehrg.
§ 118.—Spoken in a less exact sense of
half-brothers, e. g. those born to the
same father, but of different mothers,
Gen. 42, 15. 43, 3. Judg. 9, 21; or vice
versa those born of the same mother, but
by different fathers, Judg. 8, 19. These,
where there is need of greater definite-
ness, are called בֶּן־אָב, בֶּן־אֵם, Gen.
49, 8. 43, 29.—Sometimes emphat.
of full brethren, by both the father’s
and mother’s side, Gen. 42, 4. 44, 20.
Comp. Gen. 49, 5 שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי אַחִים Simeon
and Levi are true brethren, i. e. not only
by birth but also in disposition.—The
word brother is employed by the He-
brews in other and wider senses, e. g.
2. a relative, kinsman, in any degree
of blood. Gen. 14, 16 Lot his brother, pr.
his brother’s son. 13, 8. 29, 12. 15.
3. one of the same tribe, contribulis,
2 Sam. 19, 13; e. g. of the Levites, Num.
4. a fellow-countryman, popularis,
Judg. 14, 3. Ex. 2, 11. 4, 18. Spoken also
even of kindred nations, e. g. of the
Edomites and Hebrews, Gen. 9, 25. 16,
5. an ally, confederate, spoken of allied
nations, as the Tyrians and Hebrews
Am. 1, 9; or those of the same religion
6. a friend, associate; so of the friends
of Job 6, 15, and perh. also 19, 13; of
Solomon, whom Hiram calls his brother,
7. any one of the same nature, a fel-
low-man, i. q. רֵעַ, Lev. 19, 17.—Hence
preceded by אִישׁ, one—the other; Gen.
13, 11 וַיִּפָּרְדוּ אִישׁ מֵעַל אָחִיו and they
separated themselves one from the other.
26, 31. This formula is applied also to
inanimate things of the same kind in the
masculine gender, just as אִשָּׁה—אָחוֹת

line_status.note: Under the aleph of the last word the print shows two vertically stacked dots (shva), not a horizontal patach stroke, so the form is יַאְזְרֵנִי (patach only under the yod), matching Reading B; all other items in the two readings are identical and match the print.

Printed visual order (left→right) is עָטַר, עָזַר; חָצַר, חָדַר, גָּדַר — a single RTL run, so in logical order the first word is גָּדַר (with dagesh in gimel, as printed) and the last is עָטַר, i.e. Reading A's word order; Reading B has simply copied the visual order and would render reversed. But the print has a space before the colon ("Spoken :"), as in B. All vowels (qamets + patach in every word) match both readings.
Under the aleph of the final word the print shows a compound point (two shewa dots plus a short bar), i.e. hataf patah אֲ, not a plain patah אַ; so Reading B is correct.
Under the aleph of אחות the print shows a plain qamets (horizontal bar with single descender), not a hataf patah; there is no shewa pair beside it. Reading B matches.
